subject: Post-discovery: engineering lab booking and data-scope check
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex King <alex.king@neohealth.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-discovery: engineering lab booking and data-scope check

Hi Alex —

Great to meet yesterday. Per our discovery call, NeoHealth's primary goals for the lab are: validating real-time inference latency with 512 token prompts, verifying prefix caching behavior for clinical note templates, and exercising secure private networking to your VPC.

To get the engineering lab scheduled this week, can you confirm:
- who will join from NeoHealth (names + roles)
- any firewall/NAT or proxy constraints we should know about
- a representative sample size for the test dataset (rough token count / # of records)

We have two 90-minute slots available for a hands-on session where our runtime engineers will bring a small test harness:
- Wednesday 13 May, 16:00–17:30 PT
- Thursday 14 May, 09:00–10:30 PT

If neither works, propose two alternatives and we’ll accommodate. I’ve attached a short pre-lab checklist that covers network, credentials, and the minimal data artifacts we ask customers to stage.

Attachments: pre-lab-checklist.xlsx (attachment)

Thanks —
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0143

--
Note: Ben Carter will lead the runtime side if we need to deep-dive into kernel/quantization choices.

From: Alex King <alex.king@neohealth.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@neohealth.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: engineering lab booking and data-scope check

Thanks Mateo —

Appreciate the recap. Attendees from our side will be: Alex King (CTO), Emily Zhao (Lead ML Eng), and Victor Park (Infra). We have an internal security reviewer who may join briefly.

For the dataset: we can stage ~15k records (avg ~600 tokens per record) as a representative sample. Network: we can open outbound to a specific IP range and support a temporary VPN if needed.

Both slots look possible on our end but prefer Wednesday 13 May at 16:00 PT. Can you confirm who from Redwood will be on the call and whether we should prepare any service account keys ahead of time?

Also — I tried to open the checklist but our SSO blocked the download. Can you paste the small network snippet in-line?

Best,
Alex
Alex King | CTO, NeoHealth.ai
alex.king@neohealth.ai

--

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Alex King <alex.king@neohealth.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:54:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: engineering lab booking and data-scope check

Alex —

Thanks for confirming. Mateo and I will be there; I’ll cover runtime perf (kernels, KV cache) and Mateo will lead environment setup. I’m adding Evelyn Hart to the thread — she owns our security checklist and can respond to the SSO/keys question.

Short answers to Alex's questions:
- Redwood attendees: Ben Carter (Runtime Eng), Mateo Alvarez (Solutions Eng), Evelyn Hart (Security/Compliance)
- Service account: a short-lived API key is fine for the lab; if you prefer a VPN tunnel and no keys, we can run via private peering during the session. Either approach works — we’ll adapt.
- Network snippet (inline): allow outbound TLS (443) to 44.34.120.0/26 and 44.34.121.0/26; if you restrict by FQDN allow *.redwoodinference.com and api.redwoodinference.com.

If Wednesday 13 May 16:00 PT is good, I’ll lock the invite and include a small pre-built harness.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwoodinference.com

--

Thanks Ben — that looks good. Quick update: our security lead flagged a calendar conflict on Wednesday afternoon and asked if we can shift the session to Thursday morning.

Can we move to Thursday 14 May, 09:00–10:30 PT instead? Same attendees, and we’ll get the service account key created before the call if keys are preferred.

If that doesn’t work, we could also keep Wednesday and have a follow-up 30m security-only sync.

—Alex

Thursday 14 May 09:00–10:30 PT works for us. I’ve created a calendar invite and attached the minimal playbook excerpt (redwood-eng-ops-playbook.pdf) — the full checklist is in the XLSX but the excerpt covers creds, IPs, and expected artifacts.
